# Severity Service Integration in CCRS

This is a draft for ideas on integrating the Severity service into the existing complaint creation lifecycle in the CCRS repository.

## Current APIs and schemas

The Severity service is currently accessible as an API.

Reference: [PGR services README](https://github.com/egovernments/Citizen-Complaint-Resolution-System/blob/master/backend/pgr-services/README.md)

## Integration recommendation

The recommended approach is to try a synchronous integration if the Severity API takes less than 2 seconds to respond. Otherwise, try an asynchronous approach.

- We want to touch as few components as possible and, if possible, keep changes additive by extending existing functionality.
- Severity Service failures or slowness must never block submission or cause a complaint to be lost.

## Potential synchronous approach

![][image4]

**Changes required:**
- PGR service backend source code
- `egov-persister` configuration file: `local-setup/configs/egov-persister/pgr-services-persister.yml`

**Pros:**
- Easy to implement.

**Cons:**
- Synchronous.
- If the Severity service fails, severity-related fields will be empty in the database unless some mechanism is implemented to call the API later after a failure.

## Asynchronous approach (preferred)

![][image5]

**`eg_pgr_severity_v2` schema:**

![][image6]

**Note:** For simplicity, the severity labels can be stored in the existing `additionalDetails` JSONB field.

**Changes required:**
- New Severity Kafka consumer.
- Potentially, a new table for severity fields.
- New `save-pgr-severity` topic.
- `egov-persister` configuration file: `local-setup/configs/egov-persister/pgr-services-persister.yml`.
- No changes to the existing PGR service or PGR tables.

**Pros:**
- Asynchronous and parallel.
- The user does not wait for the Severity API.
- The Severity API can run in parallel with the PGR service.
